title: Melt-in-Your-Mouth Buttermilk Biscuits
subtitle: Fluffy, easy, buttery, mouthwatering biscuits you can enjoy with any meal

hero.imageAlt: Buttermilk biscuits cooling in Grandma's kitchen

story.title: The Art of Perfect Biscuits
paragraphs: There's something magical about homemade buttermilk biscuits - the way they split open with steam rising, begging for a pat of butter and honey. These biscuits are the real deal, using a technique that creates the most incredible layers.

The secret is in keeping everything cold and working quickly. I use a cheese grater to shred the butter, which creates perfect little pockets that turn into flaky layers when baked. It's like having a little piece of heaven on your breakfast table! 🧈✨

steps.title: Prep and Chill
steps.body: Preheat your oven to 450°F. Shred the stick of butter using a cheese grater and place it in the freezer while the oven heats up. This keeps it extra cold!

steps.title: Mix Gently
steps.body: Spoon flour into the bowl with the shredded butter and gently mix so the butter pieces are coated with flour. This prevents the butter from clumping together.

steps.title: Add the Buttermilk
steps.body: Pour in the cold buttermilk and stir just until a dough forms. Don't overmix - lumpy is perfectly fine!

steps.title: Work Quickly
steps.body: Sprinkle flour on the counter and dump the dough onto it. Flour your hands and gently pat and fold the dough several times to create layers. Flatten to about 1 inch thick. Work quickly to keep the dough from warming!

steps.title: Cut and Bake
steps.body: Cut out the biscuits and place them in a greased skillet or pie pan so their sides are touching. Bake for 12-16 minutes until cooked through and golden.

tips.title: Cold Everything
tips.body: Keep the dough cold and slightly sticky. This is the secret to incredibly flaky layers!

tips.title: Straight Down Cut
tips.body: Don't twist the cutter when cutting biscuits - press straight down to avoid sealing the sides.

tips.title: Sides Touching
tips.body: Place biscuits with sides touching in the pan - they support each other and rise higher!

tips.title: Hot Oven Ready
tips.body: Make sure the oven is fully preheated. You can chill the cut biscuits in the fridge while waiting!

variations.title: Cheese Biscuits
variations.body: Add ½ cup sharp cheddar cheese to the flour mixture for savory cheese biscuits.

variations.title: Herb Biscuits
variations.body: Mix in 2 tablespoons fresh chives, rosemary, or thyme for an aromatic twist.

variations.title: Sweet Biscuits
variations.body: Add 2 tablespoons sugar and a teaspoon of vanilla for a slightly sweet version.

footer.heading: Happy Baking!
footer.text: These biscuits are perfect with honey, jam, sausage gravy, or just a generous pat of butter. Pure comfort! 💕
